title: Turkish Bayraktar TB2 drones and Israeli loitering munitions shape the 2020 Karabakh war
body:
In a report published on 8 December 2020, analysts Shaan Shaikh and Wes Rumbaugh of the CSIS Missile Defense Project examined the air and missile war in Nagorno-Karabakh, which began on 27 September 2020. They described the Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 as an armed drone that Azerbaijan acquired in 2020, with reports suggesting the sale took place as recently as June 2020. The TB2 identified and targeted enemy defences and carried small guided munitions to strike targets itself. It flew too high for Armenia's short-range air defences to intercept, and its high-definition cameras also produced footage widely used for propaganda.

Azerbaijan had also bought Israeli loitering munitions before the war, among them the Harop, Orbiter and SkyStriker, which are sometimes called suicide or kamikaze drones. Early in the conflict these weapons were used against Armenia's S-300 air defences. Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev claimed that seven S-300 launchers, two guidance stations and one radar were destroyed, though the authors noted these figures may be exaggerated.

The report found that most of Armenia's air defences were obsolete Soviet-era systems that struggled against high-flying TB2s. Russian-supplied Polye-21 electronic warfare equipment disrupted Azerbaijani drone operations for only about four days. Armenia's Buk and Tor-M2KM systems arrived late and in small numbers, likely downing only a few drones, and were themselves vulnerable. Suppressing Armenian air defences, the authors wrote, amplified the effectiveness of Azerbaijan's drones.
